mint.main: Readable.mint_readable (ReadableMint.lean), proved from the raw completeness theorem ok_mint (Gen/PMint.lean, 12 paths, 1 success path mint_p11, base gas 4303 plus slot costs).
mint.who: per call: a successful mint was sent by the owner: caller = the address in the low 160 bits of slot 0 at that call (callerW message = ownerOf message state). No other minter role exists in the bytes.
mint.wait: (lastMintTimestamp).toNat + 31536000 <= block.timestamp (365 days). lastMintTimestamp = the 40 low bits of slot 11. The subtraction is checked: a block time below the last mint time reverts with Panic 0x11; a wait that is too short reverts with 0xea0c9af5 (MintWaitPeriodInProgress).
mint.cap: amount <= 10 * totalSupply / 100 (rounded down), and 10 * totalSupply < 2^256 (checked product, Panic on overflow). Above the cap: revert 0xc507dd3b (MaxInflationExceeded). MAX_INFLATION() returns 10 and MINT_WAIT_PERIOD() returns 31536000 (maxInflation_readable, mintWaitPeriod_readable).
mint.effect: slot 11 := (block.timestamp & 0xffffffffff) | (old & ~0xffffffffff); _totalSupply := old + amount (as a natural number, checked); _balances[to] := old + amount (256-bit add, no check in the bytes; mint_no_wrap: no wrap under Inv); every other slot kept; two logs in this order: Transfer(0, to, amount), Mint(to, amount) (topic 0x0f6798a560793a54c3bcfe86a93cde1e73087d944c0ea20544137d4121396885); empty output; to != 0.
mint.witness: Sanity.mint_runs: mint(2, 1) by the owner, total supply 10, last mint 0, block time 31536000 runs with no error.
mint.scope: All mint rules here are per call (mint_readable: IF one mint call ends with no error THEN ...). The ten-token audit, ENA-2: there is no sequence theorem about slot 11 or slot 4, no single theorem that no other function raises totalSupply or writes slot 11 or slot 0, and no summary of the failing side (the 11 revert paths are proved one by one). A sequence form was not added in this fix round: it needs block time in the step relation and the extra keccak facts of ENA-1.

assumptions: Sep (callKeys message): keccak mapping slots of the address words of the call do not collide (balance slots unique, allowance and nonce slots are not balance slots and not slot 4, slots 0, 1, 11 are no balance slot). Hypothesis on keccak, not proved. Used by the supply invariant, by the readable theorems of functions that write (mint_readable included) and by permit_readable. No closed instance of Sep exists (see closed_instance): it fails only on a keccak collision or preimage, about 2^-96 per fact under the random-function view, but that is a heuristic, not a proof. Read every "every message" or "every successful call" of this file as "every message whose mapping slots do not collide".

Fork range (see fork_range): every claim is for Shapella <= fork < Glamsterdam; transactions Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam. The frame-level generated theorems are proved from Shapella and do not state the upper bound; they are about the one-counter gas meter (Nat), which EthLib runs only before Glamsterdam. The EIP-8037 two-counter meter is not ported.

Transaction level: forks before Dencun. There the end of a transaction can delete an account that ran SELFDESTRUCT, and it is not proved here that the code of ENA never runs it (the library tracks instead that C is not created in the transaction and not marked for deletion, which EIP-6780 gives from Dencun).
Transaction level: Glamsterdam and later (two-counter gas meter).
Transaction level: the base case of supply_from_zero is all-zero storage; the constructor run that leaves the real start state is not linked, so nothing is proved about the real chain state.
Transaction level: NoDelegation1 at each entry into the token is assumed, not derived from a start state (no theorem that a run keeps address 1 free of delegation code).
Transaction level: the mint rules (owner only, 365 days wait, 10 percent cap) have no sequence form; they stay theorems about one call (mint_readable).
No closed instance of Sep and of any theorem under Sep (see closed_instance): the keccak facts are reduced to the 7 named facts of KeyFacts and left as a hypothesis.
NoDelegation1 is not shown to be kept by a run or by a sequence (see permit.no_delegation1).
contract_findings: SCOPE of this list: every item is read from the bytes and proved PER CALL (one successful call implies ...). No item is a theorem over a sequence of calls, and nothing here reads the live chain state (who holds a role today is not known to the proofs).

Mint, per call: a mint(to, amount) that ends with no error was sent by the address in slot 0 (the owner) at the time of that call (mint_readable). No other function reaches the mint code (read from the bytes by the ten-token audit; no single Lean theorem says "only mint raises the total supply"). No separate minter role (USDE has one, ENA does not).

How often, per call: a successful mint needs block.timestamp - lastMintTimestamp >= 31536000 (365 days) at that call and sets lastMintTimestamp to the block time (40 low bits). "At most one mint per 365 days" is the reading of this over time; it is NOT a Lean theorem (no sequence theorem about slot 11).

How much, per call: amount <= 10 * totalSupply / 100 (rounded down) at the time of the call. "The supply grows by at most 10 percent per 365 days through mint" is an inference from the two per-call rules, NOT a Lean theorem. The cap compounds (each mint raises the next cap) and a burn lowers it.
mint(to, 0) by the owner is allowed when the wait has passed, and it restarts the 365-day wait (the bytes have no amount > 0 check).
The mint time is stored in 40 bits (wraps after year 36812); the comparison uses the full block time, so there is no practical effect.
to must not be 0; totalSupply add is checked, the balance add is unchecked (safe under the supply invariant).

Owner change: two steps (Ownable2Step): transferOwnership(new) writes _pendingOwner and logs OwnershipTransferStarted; acceptOwnership by the pending owner writes _owner, clears _pendingOwner and logs OwnershipTransferred. Slots 0 and 1 keep their 96 high bits.
renounceOwnership() always reverts (proved: renounceOwnership_never; ok_renounceOwnership : False), so the mint right cannot be given up that way.
burn(amount) burns the caller's balance; burnFrom(account, amount) spends allowance (infinite allowance is not reduced). Supply moves by exactly the amount.
No pause, no blacklist, no fee, no hook: transfer/transferFrom move exactly the amount.

transaction_theorems.file: EnaVerify/Ena/Tx.lean (170 lines, 10 theorems, 1 abbrev QMsg), on the shared library TokenKit/Seq (Frame, Run, Tx, Supply)
transaction_theorems.headline: supply_any_transactions: after any finite list of transactions (Seq.Chain) that EthLib's processTransaction runs, whoever sends them, whatever they call and however deep (calls back into ENA included), C still holds the code of ENA and the supply invariant Inv C holds, when both held on the block state before the first one. Every selector is included: supply_permit (PermitSeq.lean) for permit, supply_preserved (Invariant.lean) for every other selector, mint included.
transaction_theorems.supply_message_any_depth: one call run by EthLib's processMessage, to any account and any code, at any depth: 'C holds the code of ENA and the invariant holds' is kept, with or without an error. Shapella <= fork < Glamsterdam. Assumes Seq.Sane (a call that runs at C runs CODE), Seq.Good at the start, Seq.Clean of this run with Q := QMsg fork.
transaction_theorems.supply_transaction: one whole transaction run by EthLib's processTransaction (gas purchase, EIP-7702 authorizations, the message, call or creation, refunds, fee, deletion of accounts): block state before to block state after. Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam. Assumes Seq.TxClean of this transaction and Seq.Good at the start.
transaction_theorems.supply_any_transactions: the same after any finite list of transactions (Seq.Chain), each at its own fork (Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam) and in its own block environment.
transaction_theorems.supply_from_zero: the same from the base case shape: C holds the code and every storage word of C is zero (inv_zeroBase); conclusion Inv C after the list. This is NOT the real deployment state of ENA (the constructor mints the first supply; that run is not verified).
transaction_theorems.frameKeepsR: the per-frame premise of the library (Seq.FrameKeepsR: a frame that runs CODE at C under EthLib's real runner processRunner and ends with no error keeps Inv C), proved from the existing all-selector theorems: supply_permit (PermitSeq.lean) for permit, supply_preserved (Invariant.lean) for every other selector, mint included. Shapella <= fork < Glamsterdam, any gas cap. No hypothesis on the runner is left: the STATICCALL to the ecrecover precompile is a message of the run like any other and the library induction covers it.
transaction_theorems.fork_range: transaction theorems: Fork.dencun <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam for each transaction. Message theorem: Fork.shapella <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam.
transaction_theorems.start_state: Seq.Good C CODE (Inv C) on the block state before the first transaction (assumed, see assumptions); supply_from_zero: Seq.HoldsCode plus all-zero storage of C.
transaction_theorems.older_model_kept: Seq.lean and PermitSeq.lean (inv_calls, inv_callsP, process_step, process_step_all, process_step_all_inv, calls_process, callsP_process): top-level messages only, where every other step is ASSUMED to keep the storage of C (the constructor `other` with `Untouched`). This is the weaker per-message model. It is kept because other files and the axioms list use it; the theorems of Tx.lean do not use that assumption.
transaction_theorems.mint_rules_stay_per_call: The mint rules of ENA (only the owner, at most once per 365 days, at most 10 percent of the total supply: Readable.mint_readable in ReadableMint.lean) are theorems about ONE successful call frame. No sequence form was proved: nothing here says how much the supply can grow over a list of transactions. The transaction theorems are about the supply invariant (sum of balances = totalSupply) only.

fork_range.headline: Every claim of this file is for Shapella <= fork < Glamsterdam (transactions: Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam). Nothing is claimed for Glamsterdam or later.
fork_range.why: The proofs use the one-counter gas meter (Evm fork Nat). EthLib runs that meter only before Glamsterdam; from Glamsterdam it runs the two-counter meter of EIP-8037, which is not ported.
fork_range.stated_in_the_theorem: fork < .glamsterdam is a hypothesis of: ok_permit_real, permit_readable, supply_permit, process_step_all, process_step_all_inv, permitCall_process, callsP_process, frameKeepsR, supply_message_any_depth, supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero (Tx.lean), and of every theorem of Instance.lean and PermitRun.lean that is about a run (supply_m0, ecrecover_call_runs, permit_runs, supply_permit_m1, permit_runs_inv).
fork_range.not_stated_in_the_theorem: The older generated theorems (block rules, path specs, ok_<fn>, supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, <fn>_readable, the Sanity witnesses) and the hand-written older per-message model of Seq.lean (process_step, process_step_inv, calls_process) carry only the lower bound (Shapella <= fork; Seq.lean from Shapella). They are statements about the one-counter model and are true as stated at every such fork, but they describe what EthLib really runs only before Glamsterdam. The bound was NOT added to them: it would have to come from the generators in token-kit/scripts (shared by every token, outside the scope of this fix round), and adding a hypothesis that the proofs do not use would change no proof. Read each of them with fork < Glamsterdam; every headline that reaches a message or a transaction (the lists above) states it.

closed_instance.audit: the ten-token audit, fix 5 (ENA-1): PARTLY closed
closed_instance.plain_answer: There is NO closed instance of Sep, and so no theorem under Sep (supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, supply_permit, the readable theorems of the writers, the sequence and transaction theorems) has an instance with every hypothesis proved. Each open fact of Sep says that a given slot is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a: a statement over 2^160 values of keccak. keccak is a real function here, but no proof can run it 2^160 times and no shorter argument is known (it is preimage and collision resistance). Under the usual random-function view each fact fails with chance about 2^-96.
closed_instance.state_and_call: state sState C []: one account at the contract C, every storage word 0. Call m0: allowance(K, K) sent by HOLDER, the address with the word K = 0x19e7e376e7c213b7e7e7e46cc70a5dd086daff2a (the address of the public test key 0x11...11), so the three mapping keys of the call are K, K, K.
proved_with_no_hypothesis: inv_start: the start invariant Inv holds in that state (sum of balances 0, total supply 0)
callKeys_m0, callKeys_m1: the keys of the two calls are [K, K, K]
computed by the kernel with the real keccak: allow_ne_total, nonce_ne_total, allow_ne_nonce, slots_not_fixed
sep_iff, sep_m0_iff: Sep [K, K, K] holds exactly when KeyFacts holds (both directions), so the list of 7 facts below is the whole open part and cannot be made shorter
left_as_hypothesis: KeyFacts.total: slot 4 (the total supply) is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a
KeyFacts.uniq: no address word other than K has the balance slot of K
KeyFacts.allow: the allowance slot of (K, K) is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.nonce: the nonce slot of K (mapping at slot 9) is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.slot0: slot 0 is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.slot1: slot 1 is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.slot11: slot 11 is the balance slot of no address word
closed_modulo_KeyFacts: supply_m0: every run of m0 from sState C [] that ends with no error ends in a state where Inv holds. Hypotheses: Shapella <= fork < Glamsterdam and KeyFacts; nothing else.

supply_permit_m1 (PermitRun.lean): the same for the permit call m1 under the real runner. Hypotheses: Shapella <= fork < Glamsterdam and KeyFacts; nothing else (the start invariant, NoDelegation1, the size of the call data and the selector are discharged).
permit_runs_inv: the run of permit_runs exists and, under KeyFacts, ends in a state where Inv holds.
closed_instance.not_done: No base case was added to the sequence or transaction theorems beyond the existing supply_from_zero / inv_zeroBase (all-zero storage); inv_start is that base case for the concrete state. The real chain state is not used.
closed_instance.extra_keccak_fact: The ten-token audit (ENA-1, also true for USDE): Sep says nothing about an allowance slot or a nonce slot being slot 0, 1 or 11. So a reading such as "approve or permit never changes the owner word" needs one more keccak fact per call, which is NOT in Sep and NOT proved in general. For the keys of the instance it is computed by the kernel: Instance.slots_not_fixed (the allowance slot of (K, K) and the nonce slot of K are none of 0, 1, 11).

owner_facts.source: the ten-token audit, finding ENA-9: facts about the deployed bytes that the auditor confirmed and that matter to an owner or a user. Each is per call; none is a statement about live chain state.
facts: ENA-9.1: only the address in slot 0 can mint; there is no other minter role and no other entry to the mint code (per call).
ENA-9.2: the cap compounds: each mint raises the next cap, a burn lowers it.
ENA-9.3: mint(to, 0) is allowed and restarts the 365-day wait, so the owner can use up a year of mint right with one call.

ENA-9.4: if lastMintTimestamp is above the block time the mint reverts with Panic 0x11. The first allowed mint time depends on the value the constructor stored in slot 11, which the proofs do not model and nobody read from chain here.
ENA-9.5: lastMintTimestamp keeps only 40 bits of the block time (wraps in year 36812, no practical effect).

ENA-9.6: renounceOwnership() always reverts, so the mint right cannot be dropped that way; ownership moves only by transferOwnership then acceptOwnership. transferOwnership has no zero-address check: transferOwnership(0) just clears the pending owner.
ENA-9.7: the totalSupply add in mint is checked; the receiver balance add and the totalSupply sub in burn are unchecked and safe only because sum of balances = totalSupply.
ENA-9.8: burnFrom and transferFrom do not lower an allowance of 2^256 - 1.

ENA-9.9: permit: the nonce is incremented before the ECRECOVER call; high s and a zero recovered address are rejected; the domain separator is rebuilt when chain id or address differ from the cached ones.
ENA-9.10: no pause, blacklist, fee or hook; the only outside call in the whole code is the STATICCALL to address 1.
